sentences.text: Cyphornis is a genus of prehistoric birds known for having pseudoteeth on their beaks.
The species is known with certainty only from a single, abraded fossil consisting of the proximal part of a left tarsometatarsus.
At the time of its discovery, Cyphornis was considered the largest known bird capable of flight.
Today, Cyphornis remains one of the largest known flying birds, though not the heaviest.
Huge pseudotooth wing bone fossils have also been discovered in Oregon.
The genus Cyphornis was described by Edward Drinker Cope in 1894.
The type specimen was found at Carmanah Point on Vancouver Island, Canada, near the entrance to the Juan de Fuca Strait.
The only known species within the genus is Cyphornis magnus.
The genus is placed in the order Odontopterygiformes due to uncertainty regarding its closest relatives.
Due to its fragmentary nature, Cyphornis was often allied with the enigmatic genus Cladornis.
Modern research generally classifies Cladornis as a terrestrial bird rather than a seabird.
Cyphornis was originally separated into the family Cyphornithidae along with Palaeochenoides mioceanus and Tympanonesiotes wetmorei.
The family Cyphornithidae is almost certainly a junior synonym of the family Pelagornithidae.
The parent group of the genus Cyphornis is the family Pelagornithidae.
The fossil deposits were initially dated to the Eocene but are usually assigned to the Early Miocene.
Fossils found in Washington County and near Mist date from the Eo-Oligocene boundary.
Cyphornis lived during the Rupelian to Chattian stages, approximately 33.9 to 23.04 million years ago.
